title: Deadline and Border
premise: Ada Eastwick, a whistle-blower living under four names, has built a career on cases no one wants attributed—until a burner phone that shouldn't exist rings with the voice of her presumed-dead handler, Marek, who claims he's alive inside a Frankfurt extraction pipeline and needs her to pull out a defector carrying proof of a market-manipulation scheme before markets open. Ada realizes the defector may be bait designed to flush her out, and that her own survival was traded years ago in a deal she never knew she made. Choosing loyalty to a ghost over the truth that could free her, Ada runs the extraction anyway, discovers Marek is both dead and the trap's architect—a recording weaponized by his killers—and burns her fourth name to expose the scheme at the opening bell, surviving as no one at all.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former financial-crimes analyst who spent a decade inside compliance departments before walking away with nothing but his notes. He writes thrillers about people who trade their identities for the truth and are never quite sure they got a fair price.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Living quietly in Rotterdam as 'Ingrid Voss,' Ada takes an anonymous document-review job, until a burner phone buried in her emergency kit—the number only Marek ever knew—rings with his voice begging for extraction. The emotional beat is vertigo: grief reopening, paranoia sharpening, and the first crack in the invisibility she's paid everything to maintain.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Debt
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada's POV with intercepted surveillance reports. Ada traces the defector, Lena Brandt, through Frankfurt's gray-market intermediaries while reconstructing how each of her four names was burned—and realizing someone fed her locations to keep her moving toward this exact night. The beat is dread compounding into resolve: belonging was always the lure.

chapters.title: Extraction at the Bell
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, real-time across one night. She pulls Lena from a safehouse as private security closes in, and at the moment of handoff discovers Marek's voice is a synthesized recording—the defector is the trigger for a coordinated short position timed to market open. The climax: Ada must choose between escaping with Lena or hijacking the kill switch mid-broadcast.

chapters.title: No One at All
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, aftermath. She releases the manipulation evidence under none of her names, letting the markets and the conspirators burn together, then sits with Lena in a train station watching dawn arrive—two women who no longer exist anywhere official. The resolution lands the theme: survival cost her every name, but truth finally bought her something to belong to.
